title: ResizeObserver
learningObjectives: Explain resizeobserver and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: ResizeObserver reports changes to an element's content or border box size. It is useful when a component needs to respond to its own dimensions rather than only viewport changes. Disconnect the observer during cleanup and avoid resize feedback loops.
understand.whyItMatters: Component size can change because of parent layout, fonts, or content, even when the viewport does not change. ResizeObserver provides a direct signal for those changes.
understand.analogy: A ResizeObserver is a measuring assistant that reports when a component's box changes size.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The callback receives measurements when the observed element's size changes.

examples.code: const panel=document.querySelector('#panel');const observer=new ResizeObserver(entries=>{for(const entry of entries)console.log(entry.contentRect.width)});if(panel)observer.observe(panel);// cleanup: observer.disconnect();
examples.explanation: The callback receives measurements when the observed element's size changes.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Build a responsive widget that reports its own width. Avoid changing the observed size in a way that creates an endless resize loop.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.
